newsitem.title: USA: Clinton aims to raise $200 mln leasing SPR space.
newsitem.headline: Clinton aims to raise $200 mln leasing SPR space.

text.p: The Clinton administration proposed Thursday to raise $200 million between 1999 and 2002 by leasing out excess space in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
As expected, the White House's budget included a provision to lease space in the SPR caverns, a move which the Energy Department first proposed last year but Congress never had time to debate.
According to the, leased storage would bring in $14 million in the 1999 fiscal year, which begins October 1, 1998, $37 million in 2000, $67 million 2001 and $83 million in 2002.

The administration's estimates were more generous than calculations by the Congressional Budget Office, which last year estimated that leasing excess space in the SPR would yield less than $10 million a year.
Congressional and Energy Department sources said it would probably take a few years for such a program to get off the ground.
It would require a marketing effort by the administration and negotiations with foreign countries which might want to store oil in the U.S. for energy emergencies, they said.
The reserve has a capacity of 680 million barrels, following the recent closure of one of its caverns, and currently holds about 564 million barrels.
